coverage: All three plays and 26 local sections in both English editions: named cast, separate choruses, individual elders, speaking roles, family and mythological references. Exact reviewed aliases and selected contextual references.

entities.name: Agamemnon
entities.body: The king of Argos, commander of the Greek expedition to Troy, and husband of Clytemnestra.

entities.name: Clytemnestra
entities.body: Agamemnon’s wife and queen of Argos, mother of Orestes, Electra and Iphigenia.

entities.name: Orestes
entities.body: The son of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, and brother of Electra.

entities.name: Cassandra
entities.body: The Trojan princess and prophetess brought back as Agamemnon’s captive.

entities.name: Aegisthus
entities.body: Clytemnestra’s lover and the son of Thyestes, from the rival branch of Agamemnon’s family.

entities.name: Electra
entities.body: The daughter of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, and sister of Orestes.

entities.name: Apollo
entities.body: The god of prophecy, worshipped at Delphi and also called Loxias or Phoebus.

entities.name: Athena
entities.body: The patron goddess of Athens, daughter of Zeus, also called Pallas.

entities.name: The Furies
entities.body: The ancient avenging goddesses who punish violations of family bonds.

entities.name: The Argive elders
entities.body: The elders of Argos who form the chorus in Agamemnon.

entities.name: The libation bearers
entities.body: The enslaved women of the palace who accompany Electra and form the second play’s chorus.

entities.name: The watchman
entities.body: The palace watchman waiting for the beacon that will signal news from Troy.

entities.name: The herald
entities.body: The messenger returning from the Greek expedition to Troy.

entities.name: The leader of the Argive elders
entities.body: The spokesman for the elders of Argos.

entities.name: Argive elder 1
entities.body: One of the elders separately voicing advice during the palace crisis.

entities.name: Argive elder 2
entities.body: One of the elders separately voicing advice during the palace crisis.

entities.name: Argive elder 3
entities.body: One of the elders separately voicing advice during the palace crisis.

entities.name: Argive elder 4
entities.body: One of the elders separately voicing advice during the palace crisis.

entities.name: Argive elder 5
entities.body: One of the elders separately voicing advice during the palace crisis.

entities.name: Argive elder 6
entities.body: One of the elders separately voicing advice during the palace crisis.

entities.name: Argive elder 7
entities.body: One of the elders separately voicing advice during the palace crisis.

entities.name: Argive elder 8
entities.body: One of the elders separately voicing advice during the palace crisis.

entities.name: Argive elder 9
entities.body: One of the elders separately voicing advice during the palace crisis.

entities.name: Argive elder 10
entities.body: One of the elders separately voicing advice during the palace crisis.

entities.name: Argive elder 11
entities.body: One of the elders separately voicing advice during the palace crisis.

entities.name: Pylades
entities.body: Orestes’s companion, son of Strophius of Phocis.

entities.name: Kilissa
entities.body: Orestes’s old nurse in the palace of Argos.

entities.name: The palace doorkeeper
entities.body: The servant who answers the travelers’ knock at the palace.

entities.name: Aegisthus’s servant
entities.body: The palace servant who calls for help from Clytemnestra’s quarters.

entities.name: The Pythian priestess
entities.body: Apollo’s priestess at the oracle of Delphi.

entities.name: The first Fury
entities.body: One of the avenging goddesses, speaking separately as they wake.

entities.name: The Athenian jurors
entities.body: The twelve Athenian citizens assembled by Athena to hear the case.

entities.name: The Athenian escort
entities.body: The women and children who form the ceremonial procession at the end of the trilogy.

entities.name: The palace maidens
entities.body: Clytemnestra’s attendants carrying the purple robes for Agamemnon’s reception.

entities.name: Atreus
entities.body: The father of Agamemnon and Menelaus, and brother of Thyestes.

entities.name: Thyestes
entities.body: Atreus’s brother and rival, and father of Aegisthus.

entities.name: Thyestes’s children
entities.body: The children of Thyestes recalled in the account of the family’s older crimes.

entities.name: Menelaus
entities.body: Agamemnon’s brother and Helen’s husband, a leader of the Greek expedition.

entities.name: Helen
entities.body: Menelaus’s wife, whose departure with Paris lies behind the Trojan War.

entities.name: Paris
entities.body: The Trojan prince who takes Helen from Menelaus, also called Alexander.

entities.name: Priam
entities.body: The king of Troy and father of Paris and Cassandra.

entities.name: Tyndareus
entities.body: Clytemnestra’s father.

entities.name: Leda
entities.body: Clytemnestra’s mother.

entities.name: Calchas
entities.body: The seer who interprets signs for the Greek army at Troy.

entities.name: Iphigenia
entities.body: The daughter of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra recalled in the account of the expedition’s departure.

entities.name: Odysseus
entities.body: The Greek commander praised by Agamemnon for his loyalty during the war.

entities.name: Geryon
entities.body: The three-bodied mythical figure used in Clytemnestra’s comparison.

entities.name: Strophius
entities.body: The ruler in Phocis who is caring for Orestes, and father of Pylades.

entities.name: Asclepius
entities.body: The divine healer famed for restoring the dead to life.

entities.name: Heracles
entities.body: The hero, son of Alcmena, cited as someone who endured servitude.

entities.name: Alcmena
entities.body: The mother of Heracles.

entities.name: Itys
entities.body: The child mourned in the mythical nightingale’s song.

entities.name: Scylla, the sea monster
entities.body: The monster feared by sailors, used in Cassandra’s comparison.

entities.name: Scylla, the king’s daughter
entities.body: The daughter who betrays her father for Minos in the chorus’s story.

entities.name: Chryseis
entities.body: The Trojan captive associated with Agamemnon, invoked as a type of his wartime lovers.

entities.name: Tantalus
entities.body: An ancestor of the royal house of Atreus.

entities.name: Pleisthenes
entities.body: An ancestral name used for the royal family of Agamemnon.

entities.name: Pelops
entities.body: The father of Atreus and Thyestes, an ancestor of the royal house.

entities.name: Orpheus
entities.body: The legendary musician whose song charms its listeners.

entities.name: Althea
entities.body: The mother in the story of a son’s life bound to a burning brand.

entities.name: Althea’s son
entities.body: The son whose life is bound to a piece of wood in the chorus’s story.

entities.name: Minos
entities.body: The Cretan king for whom Scylla betrays her father.

entities.name: Scylla’s father
entities.body: The king whose magical lock of hair is cut by his daughter Scylla.

entities.name: Perseus
entities.body: The mythical hero invoked as a model of resolve.

entities.name: Delphos
entities.body: The legendary king who welcomes Apollo to Delphi.

entities.name: Pentheus
entities.body: The king associated with opposition to Dionysus, recalled by the priestess.

entities.name: Phineus
entities.body: The king whose food is seized by the Harpies in the mythical comparison.

entities.name: Ixion
entities.body: The mythical figure whose purification is recalled as a precedent.

entities.name: Theseus
entities.body: The legendary Athenian king associated with the conflict against the Amazons.

entities.name: Aegeus
entities.body: Theseus’s father.

entities.name: Pheres
entities.body: The king whose household is recalled in the story of Apollo and the Fates.

entities.name: Erechtheus
entities.body: An ancient king and hero of Athens.

entities.name: Cranaos
entities.body: A legendary early king whose descendants stand for the Athenians.

entities.name: Zeus
entities.body: The chief Olympian god, invoked as guardian of justice and hospitality.

entities.name: Pan
entities.body: The god of shepherds and wild places.

entities.name: Artemis
entities.body: The goddess of the hunt, invoked in the account of the Greek fleet.

entities.name: Hephaestus
entities.body: The god of fire, named in the description of the beacon signal.

entities.name: Hermes
entities.body: The messenger god, son of Zeus and Maia, who also guides souls.

entities.name: Ares
entities.body: The god of war.

entities.name: Persephone
entities.body: The queen of the underworld.

entities.name: Maia
entities.body: Hermes’s mother.

entities.name: Themis
entities.body: The goddess of divine order, named among the early holders of Delphi’s oracle.

entities.name: Phoebe
entities.body: The Titan goddess who passes the Delphic oracle to Apollo.

entities.name: Earth
entities.body: The primordial goddess named as Delphi’s first prophetic power.

entities.name: Dionysus
entities.body: The god of wine and ecstatic worship, called Bacchus here.

entities.name: Poseidon
entities.body: The god of the sea.

entities.name: Hera
entities.body: Zeus’s wife, invoked as a guardian of marriage.

entities.name: Aphrodite
entities.body: The goddess of love.

entities.name: Leto
entities.body: Apollo’s mother.

entities.name: Cronos
entities.body: The Titan who is Zeus’s father.

entities.name: The Sun
entities.body: The all-seeing sun invoked as a divine witness.

entities.name: Night
entities.body: The primordial goddess, mother of the Furies.

entities.name: Justice
entities.body: Justice personified as a daughter of Zeus.

entities.name: Persuasion
entities.body: The divine power of persuasion invoked by Athena.

entities.name: The Fates
entities.body: The goddesses who determine the allotted course of lives.

entities.name: The Gorgons
entities.body: The terrifying mythical beings used in comparisons with the avenging goddesses.

entities.name: The Harpies
entities.body: The winged creatures who snatch Phineus’s food in the myth.

entities.name: The nymphs
entities.body: The nature spirits worshipped at the Corycian cave.

entities.name: The Amazons
entities.body: The women warriors recalled in the account of Athens’s past.

entities.name: Inachus
entities.body: The river god to whom Orestes dedicates a lock of hair.

entities.name: Admetus
entities.body: The son of Pheres whose escape from death is recalled in the exchange about Apollo and the Fates.

entities.name: Ate
entities.body: The divine personification of ruin and destructive delusion.

entities.name: Zephyr
entities.body: The west wind, named in the account of Helen’s voyage.
